hook: Sepp Hochreiter's 1991 diploma thesis at the Technical University of Munich diagnosed why deep and recurrent neural networks of the time failed to learn long-range dependencies, an analysis now known as the vanishing gradient problem. Working with his advisor Jurgen Schmidhuber, he developed Long Short-Term Memory networks as a solution, publishing the architecture in Neural Computation in 1997. LSTM became the dominant approach to sequence modeling for two decades, powering speech recognition and machine translation systems before the rise of Transformer models. After research positions at the University of Colorado Boulder and the Technical University of Berlin, Hochreiter joined Johannes Kepler University Linz, where he directed the Institute of Bioinformatics from 2006 and has led the Institute for Machine Learning since 2018. He also works on applying machine learning to genomics and other bioinformatics problems. In 2021 he received the IEEE Computational Intelligence Society Neural Networks Pioneer Award. He later founded NXAI, a Linz-based company building xLSTM, an extended memory architecture positioned as an alternative to Transformer models for sequence and time-series tasks.

quick_facts: Head of the Institute for Machine Learning at Johannes Kepler University Linz
Co-invented Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks with Jurgen Schmidhuber, published in Neural Computation in 1997
Identified the vanishing gradient problem in recurrent neural networks in his 1991 diploma thesis at the Technical University of Munich
Founder and Chief Scientist of NXAI, a Linz-based company building xLSTM memory architectures
Received the IEEE Computational Intelligence Society Neural Networks Pioneer Award in 2021
Also researches machine learning applications in bioinformatics and genomics

achievements.title: Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM)
achievements.impact: Co-developed with Jurgen Schmidhuber and published in 1997, LSTM solved the vanishing gradient problem that limited earlier recurrent neural networks and became the dominant architecture for sequence modeling tasks such as speech recognition and machine translation for two decades.

achievements.title: Diagnosis of the vanishing gradient problem
achievements.impact: His 1991 diploma thesis explained why deep and recurrent networks struggled to learn long-range dependencies, a diagnosis that shaped later deep learning architecture design.
